title: After the worst years, what came next?
summary_lines: The S&P 500 has finished the year in the red 30 times since 1928.

facts.post:
The S&P 500 has finished the year in the red 30 times since 1928.
The year after, it went up 21 of those 30 times.

Japan's the exception. After the Nikkei fell 38.7% in 1990, it took 34 years to close above its 1989 level.

Anyone else hold through 2022 (-19.4%)?
facts.reply: We ran the same numbers for Europe, the UK, Japan and Korea too. Price indexes, dividends not included.

facts.s3_note: It fell 38.7% in 1990. Averages aren't promises.
